extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and grant applicants preparing NIH Data Management & Sharing (DMS) Plans for NIH-funded applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing a Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan to satisfy the NIH 2023/2026 DMS Policy requirements for grant applications, including special considerations for human and genomic data, repository selection, timing, and justification for any limits on sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum appropriate sharing of scientific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Will there be maximum appropriate sharing of scientific data underlying peer-reviewed publications and other findings resulting from the work supported by this award (including preprints, refereed papers reported at conferences, and other findings)? [YES/NO]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the 2023 DMS Policy NIH expects researchers to maximize the appropriate sharing of scientific data, taking into account legal, ethical, or technical issues that may limit extent of sharing. See 'Maximum Appropriate Sharing of Scientific Data' for examples of justifiable and not-justifiable limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of sharing for data underlying publications and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific data underlying peer-reviewed publications be shared by the time of publication or, for other findings, by the end of the period of performance, which includes no-cost extensions? [YES/NO]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no or if sharing will be limited in other ways, explain in element 4 (limitations). NIH expects sharing by publication or by end of performance period unless justifiable limitations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of availability of shared scientific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Will shared scientific data be made available for at least as long as required by applicable data repository policies and/or journal policies? [YES/NO]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no, describe limitations and the ethical, legal, or technical factors that limit sharing (see element 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for limitations on sharing (300 words maximum)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you answered 'no' to elements 1, 2, or 3, or if you anticipate that sharing will be limited in some other way, please describe these limitations and the ethical, legal, or technical factors for them. Your response should specify a particular reason(s) for limiting sharing. [300 words maximum]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide compelling, specific justifications. Examples of justifiable and not-justifiable factors are provided on the NIH page to guide acceptable reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of privacy, rights, and confidentiality for human participant data
rubrics_metrics.description: If scientific data derived from human research participants will be shared, will privacy, rights, and confidentiality of participants be protected as outlined in NOT-OD-22-213, including whether any scientific data will be shared using access controls? [YES/NO/Not Applicable]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether access controls will be used. Consult 'Principles and Best Practices for Protecting Participant Privacy' and relevant notices for additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: List key types of scientific data and proposed repositories (table, 100 words maximum)
rubrics_metrics.description: In table format list the key types of scientific data anticipated to be generated during the project, including the species and modality, if known (e.g., 'human genomic data,' 'rat functional magnetic resonance imaging data') and the repository or example repository where the scientific data may be managed and shared. [100 words maximum]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH recognizes not all data types expected will meet the definition of scientific data or be anticipated in advance. If a data type does not appear, it does not imply it will not be shared. NIH expects use of established repositories for preserving and sharing scientific data when available; consult 'Selecting a Data Repository.'

rubrics_metrics.name: GDS-specific: share large-scale human genomic data in NIH-designated repository
rubrics_metrics.description: For studies subject to the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (GDS): Will you share all large-scale human genomic and associated data in a NIH-designated repository according to the accelerated timelines expected in the GDS Policy? [YES/NO/Not Applicable]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'no,' address in element 4 (limitations). Consult 'Where to Submit Genomic Data' and 'Data Submission and Release Expectations.' Share human genomic data according to documented expectations or by the end of the performance period, whichever comes first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-human genomic data submission and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For Non-human genomic data: you may submit data to any widely used repository and should share non-human genomic data as soon as possible, but no later than the time of an associated publication, or end of the performance period, whichever is first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult repository guidance for acceptable repositories for non-human genomic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Certification readiness for large-scale human genomic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you anticipate that when sharing large-scale human genomic data that you will be able to meet the expectations of the Institutional Certification in the GDS Policy? [YES/NO/Not Applicable]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'no,' address in element 4. Consult 'Completing an Institutional Certification Form' for different versions based on source of NIH funding, sample collection date, and consent status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of justifiable factors for limiting scientific data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples that may justify limiting sharing include: informed consent will not permit or will limit scope/extent of sharing and future research use; existing consent prohibits sharing or limits scope/extent; privacy or safety risks would be compromised or place participants at greater risk of re-identification or harm and protective measures would be insufficient; explicit federal, state, local, or Tribal law prohibits disclosure; restrictions imposed by agreements (third party funders, partners, repositories, HIPAA covered entities under a data use agreement, licensing limitations); datasets cannot practically be digitized with reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe foreseeable limitations in the DMS Plan and provide a compelling rationale for limiting scientific data sharing when one or more of these factors apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of reasons generally not justifiable for limiting sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons that would generally not be justifiable include: data are considered to be too small; data that researchers anticipate will not be widely used; data are not thought to have a suitable repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using these reasons as primary justification for limiting sharing; provide stronger, policy-aligned rationales if limiting sharing is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to use established repositories when available
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects the use of established repositories for preserving and sharing scientific data when they are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 'Selecting a Data Repository' for information on choosing an appropriate repository and for repository-specific preservation/sharing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMS Plan submission location and budget information
rubrics_metrics.description: DMS Plans should be included within the 'Other Plan(s)' field on the PHS 398 Research Plan or PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form as indicated in the Application Instructions. A brief summary and associated costs should be submitted as part of the budget and budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Budgeting for Data Management and Sharing' and the Application Instructions for details on formatting and cost presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment standard: adequacy, completeness, and acceptability of DMS Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Institute or Center (IC) program staff assess DMS Plans to ensure plan elements are adequately addressed, including any justifications for limiting data sharing. Applications selected for funding will only be funded if the DMS Plan is complete and acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers are not asked to comment on the DMS Plan and the plan is not factored into the Overall Impact score, unless sharing data is integral to the project design and specified in the funding opportunity. For budget assessment by peer reviewers, consult 'Budgeting for Data Management and Sharing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising DMS Plans pre-award and post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-Award: If the DMS Plan in the application cannot be approved, applicants will be notified during the Just-in-Time (JIT) process and may need to submit a revised DMS Plan after discussing with Program Officer/Grants Management Specialist. Post-Award: Plans may need updating if data types change or a more appropriate repository becomes available; updates require funding ICO approval and will be monitored during the annual RPPR process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 2.5.1 Just-in-Time Procedures and consult Program Officer as needed when revising plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required format: use 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format (timing for acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare your DMS Plan using the required 2026 Pilot DMS Plan Format Page (DOCX). The 2026 Pilot format is recommended and required for due dates on or after May 25, 2026. NIH will accept both the 2023 and 2026 formats for due dates prior to May 25, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If just starting, NIH recommends using the simplified 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format. The format document includes the elements/questions applicants must address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of GDS-specific considerations within the DMS Plan when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application is subject to NIH’s Genomic Data Sharing (GDS) Policy, you must also address GDS-specific considerations within the DMS Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 'Developing Genomic Data Sharing Plans', 'Where to Submit Genomic Data', and 'Data Submission and Release Expectations' for GDS-related requirements and timelines.
